The primitives establish the rigorous foundation for Fubini's theorem on product spaces. Starting with the rectangle covering property, we show that any measurable set can be approximated by countable unions of rectangles with finite measure. Then, using the monotone class theorem, we prove that the class of sets satisfying Fubini's equality is closed under limits, thus extending the result from rectangles to all measurable sets. The product formula emerges as a key computational tool, allowing us to separate integrals over different factors. These results guarantee interchangeability of iterated integrals under σ-finiteness, enabling efficient computation of high-dimensional expectations in probabilistic models.
